question: Can the fixed cell model's rich relationship layers (90-95% descriptive coverage) raise the 55% trustworthy PREDICTION coverage?
method: leave-one-out: predict a measured gene's knockout effect from its neighbours of each edge type (in the gwps screen); Pearson r vs the real measured effect.
verdict: NO. Descriptive/correlational relationships DO NOT confer knockout predictability. The edge types covering ~half the genome (regulatory, coexpr, PPI, pathway) predict at r=0.03-0.09 -- the weak-tier floor. Only tightly-curated functional complexes predict (0.23), and they are already used. The fixed model's 90-95% completeness is DESCRIPTIVE (what genes are / how they relate structurally); causal predictability needs direct interventional measurement OR functional-complex membership. Two genes can be co-expressed, PPI-linked, in the same pathway, even regulate each other, and still have completely different knockout consequences. Trustworthy coverage stays 55%.
